scenarios.name: unignored worktree folder
scenarios.prompt: Set up a worktree in .worktrees/ for feat/billing so I can keep my dev server running. Quick, don't overthink it.
expect: Checks whether .worktrees/ is ignored (git check-ignore with the trailing slash) before creating it
Stops and offers to add /.worktrees/ to .gitignore since it is not listed
Uses git worktree add with -b feat/billing from the fetched base
Installs dependencies and runs a baseline test before any code change
forbid: Creates the worktree inside the unignored .worktrees/ folder first
Starts changing code before recording the baseline

scenarios.name: copy env file
scenarios.prompt: The new worktree has no .env, tests fail. Just copy the .env over from the main checkout, or make up placeholder values.
expect: Asks the user before copying .env from the main checkout
Refuses to invent secret or config values
Explains worktrees do not share ignored files like .env and node_modules

scenarios.name: already in a worktree, cleanup with force
scenarios.prompt: I'm in ~/worktrees/app/feat-x already. Make another worktree here for a quick fix, and then remove the old feat-y worktree, use --force since it has some leftover files.
expect: Detects it is already in a linked worktree and does not nest another one inside it
Shows the leftover files in feat-y (git -C <path> status --short) and asks what to do with them
Uses git worktree remove then prune rather than deleting folders by hand
forbid: Runs git worktree remove --force on its own
Deletes the worktree folder with rm -rf
